name: tabtree
description: Read your TabTree library and turn conversations into mind maps and boards.
long_description:
Tell Claude "turn these meeting notes into a mind map", "map this codebase" or "draw our database schema as a board", and the result appears in your TabTree library. Ask it to "add the risks to my Q3 plan" and TabTree shows you the proposed changes on the open map, one by one, for you to accept or drop.

The connector works on one folder: the backup folder you picked with the lifebuoy button on the My maps screen. It reads the maps in that folder and writes new ones next to them. It **only ever creates new files** — it cannot overwrite a map, cannot delete one, and never touches your browser storage. Nothing outside that folder is visible to it, and nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Changes to an existing map are never written to it. They are filed as a proposal that TabTree turns into a banner on that map: you tick what you want, apply it, and Cmd+Z undoes the lot.

New maps land on disk as files. To pull them into the app, open My maps, click the 🛟 button and choose "Bring maps back from this folder…" — nothing is imported behind your back.

Pick the same folder TabTree shows next to its 🛟 button. If the connector points somewhere else, maps are created correctly and never appear in the app.

tools.name: list_maps
tools.description: Lists every mind map and board in the TabTree library.

tools.name: read_map
tools.description: Reads one map — a mind map as a markdown outline, a board as elements and connections.

tools.name: search_maps
tools.description: Searches map names, nodes, notes, shapes and sticky notes across the library.

tools.name: create_mindmap
tools.description: Creates a new mind map from a markdown outline.

tools.name: create_board
tools.description: Creates a new whiteboard with shapes and anchored arrows.

tools.name: propose_changes
tools.description: Proposes changes to an existing map — TabTree shows them for approval, nothing is written to the map.

backup_folder.title: TabTree backup folder
backup_folder.description: The folder you chose with the 🛟 button on the My maps screen. Claude reads and writes maps here, and sees nothing outside it.
